quido.name: Quido S.r.l.
quido.context: AI platform for private equity, M&A and investment banking
quido.contribution: I came in to help with the frontend and the interface, and within days I was proposing bigger changes. I rebuilt the platform from scratch and we shipped it in time for the investor call: they gave the go-ahead, and the projects that followed started from there. Now I decide with them what is worth building, and I set up the tooling the team works with.

recrowd.name: Recrowd S.r.l.
recrowd.contribution: Two years across their platforms, from the landing page to the investor area. The back-office already existed and we rebuilt it: we wanted marketing and customer success to work in it without asking a developer, and sensitive operations to go through 2FA. Their designer owned the design system; I took features end to end, frontend and backend.

othersideTechnology.name: Otherside Technology S.r.l.
othersideTechnology.context: Software house building tailored AI solutions
othersideTechnology.contribution: I worked on CloTU, the product companies use to query their own documents through dedicated agents. I handled the frontend and the interface: permissions across four levels, from the administrator down to a single member of a department, company access through SSO, and a different theme per customer. I designed the permission model together with the backend engineer.

brainplatform.name: Brainplatform S.r.l.
brainplatform.context: Development and design agency for digital products
brainplatform.contribution: I rebuilt a client's internal platform from scratch, with Fluent UI because the people using it all day already live inside Microsoft tools. Then two smaller dashboards, the first becoming the reusable base for the second. Their technicians make far fewer mistakes now, and they kept asking me for more. A colleague owned the backend; I taught the intern the frontend side.

studioBargiggia.name: Studio Bargiggia
studioBargiggia.contribution: They needed to update collaborators and managed buildings constantly, so I proposed a CMS instead of a site someone has to touch every time. They already had a VPS, so I put Strapi on it and added no running cost. I migrated the old site's content myself. Today they update it on their own.

anonymous.name: Anonymous
anonymous.context: Private platform for a field sales network
anonymous.contribution: The client brought the requirements, and we went through them together to work out what was feasible and what it would cost. The agents work from a tablet, so a check-in only counts if you are actually standing in front of the shop, and the quote comes out as a PDF ready for WhatsApp. Today domain, hosting and database cost them nothing, and they already know the threshold where that stops.

ravenn.name: Ravenn S.r.l.
ravenn.context: Logistics and hospitality platform for events
ravenn.contribution: I came in as a fullstack developer to support the product: maintenance, bugs, and whatever came down from the CEO. I came back a second time for something bigger, the area reserved for event staff, password-protected and with a path of its own, separate from the attendees'. I built it with another developer and closed the collaboration when it was done.

fastmemo.name: Fast Memo - Notes in one click
fastmemo.contribution: A notes app that runs on mobile and desktop and that you can keep on a server of your own. It has webhooks, dictation, and a model that runs locally. Open source, over a thousand downloads.

coolifyManager.name: Coolify Manager
coolifyManager.context: Mobile app and Chrome extension for Coolify servers
coolifyManager.contribution: An app for keeping an eye on a Coolify server from your phone, when you are away from the desk. Built on its REST API, it works with both the hosted and the self-hosted version. Over a thousand downloads.

forfettarioControl.name: Forfettario Control
forfettarioControl.context: App concept for Italian flat-tax freelancers
forfettarioControl.contribution: A concept that stopped at the design. Invoices and deadlines sorted by urgency rather than by date, drawn in Figma. It never became an app.

coffeeNotesLab.name: Coffee Notes Lab
coffeeNotesLab.context: A log of espresso tastings and home experiments
coffeeNotesLab.contribution: Where I write down the espressos I try. I built it to work on an interface with no client attached, mostly the /photos section.
